Cli_HelpText:
CKToolkit - Celtic Kings: Rage of War Integrated Toolkit
Usage: CKToolkit.exe [command] [options]

Available commands:
  apply               Apply configuration to game files
  restore --all       Normalise and reverse all patches to vanilla
  verify              Verify file patch state and configuration consistency (read-only)
  perf get            Display current performance patch settings
  perf set            Update performance patch settings (config only)
  lang list           List all available language packs (built-in and external)
  lang install        Set language pack to install (--pack <id> [--font <face>])
  lang uninstall      Uninstall language pack (restore vanilla game language)
  lang import         Safely import a language pack folder (--src <dir> [--overwrite])
  lang export-template Export language pack translation skeleton template (--out <dir> [--template <lang>])
  trainer list-cheats List all cheat definitions and default key bindings
  trainer list-tweaks List all gameplay tweaks, groups, and ranges
  trainer set         Update trainer settings (--cheat <id>=on|off --key <id>=<k> --param <id>.<n>=<v> --tweak <id>=<v> --numpad on|off)
  trainer apply       Apply trainer configuration to game files
  save list           List profiles and saves (optional --profile <profile>)
  save export         Export a save (--profile <profile> --name <save> --out <file.cksave>)
  save import         Import into the next free slot (--profile <profile> --archive <file.cksave>)
  save delete         Protected-delete a save (--profile <profile> --name <save>)
  save player get/set Read or edit player name, color, and nation
  save stats get/set  Read or edit profile-page results, rating, preferences, and totals
  profile             Full diagnostics run: injected layer + sampler + debugger, one folder (--mode launch|attach|wait --no-inject --hz <n> --log-dir <dir> --speed <n> --catch-crash on|off --full-dump --detail on|off --stack-depth <n> --speed-method hotkey|console --seconds <n> --segment <n> --out <file> --process <name>)
  run                 Launch or attach with diagnostics [--plain|--watch|--attach] [--watch-seconds <n>]
  status              Inspect game path and patch status (read-only)
  --help, -h          Show this help message
  --version, -v       Show version information

Global options:
  --game <dir>        Override game installation directory
  --config <path>     Specify configuration file path
  --json              Output structured JSON result

Gui_Trainer_Hint: The In-Game Panel is the main way to use the trainer: open it during a game and click a cheat, and the script runs immediately. Key bindings are optional — the engine only has 20 usable key ids and the game itself takes most of them, so the panel does not depend on them. Values and keys are still written into the game's own files; the panel talks to the running game only while it is open and stops the moment you close it (see AGENTS.md §2.9). Click Configure or the parameter cell to adjust values and select units visually. Hover a row for its description.
Gui_Trainer_TweaksWarning: Warning: population, training speed, army size, and mass spawning multiply the live object count together. Beyond the 2004 engine's design envelope the game may stutter badly, freeze, or crash. The trainer allows out-of-spec play but cannot guarantee the engine will sustain it.
Gui_Trainer_TweaksScopeNotice: Scope note: {0} of these settings support owner-aware splitting and are applied through the .cktw patch instead of the shared data.pak. They take effect in single-player and multiplayer alike, but in multiplayer each client applies its own self scope, which desyncs the simulation. The Global values settings below are still written to data.pak and apply to both sides.
Gui_Trainer_TweaksGlobalLabel: Global values (no owner-aware hook yet - applies to both sides and in multiplayer)

Trainer_Cheat_gold_fill_Description: Refills each friendly settlement's gold to that settlement's current storage cap (max_gold). The cap itself cannot be raised by script. Non-stock or explicitly scoped settlement-cap values are applied by .cktw to both existing and newly created settlements, in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer this desyncs the simulation.
Trainer_Cheat_food_fill_Description: Refills each friendly settlement's food to its storage cap (max_food).
Trainer_Cheat_population_boost_Descripti: Directly adds population to every friendly town and village. Income is calculated as population × production rate ÷ 100 (starting at Celtic kings.exe 0x502740) and does not consult the population cap, so more population produces more income. AddToPopulation does not check the cap either (0x504312 adds directly), making this the only way to exceed a population cap embedded in a map. The engine removes 10% of the excess every 4 seconds; to retain the added population, open Game Settings → Economy and set Over-Cap Population Loss Interval to a very large value.
Trainer_Cheat_loyalty_max_Description: Sets every friendly settlement's loyalty to 100 to prevent rebellion.
Trainer_Cheat_production_boost_Descripti: Sets friendly settlements' gold and food production rates to the chosen value (the stock base values are 24 / 20).
Trainer_Cheat_heal_army_Description: Fully heals all friendly units (Heal never exceeds a unit's maxhealth).
Trainer_Cheat_buff_army_Description: Adds attack, defense, and health bonuses only to existing friendly units; computer players are completely unaffected. This uses the engine's own unit-bonus mechanism (Unit::AddBonus, originally used for hero auras and item bonuses). The bonus is attached to each unit object rather than its class definition. By contrast, the unit-stat multipliers on the Game Settings tab modify data/classes/*.sc.xml, of which the whole game has only one copy, so they strengthen both sides; use this hotkey for a one-sided advantage. Each unit is buffed only once (buffed units are placed in the trainerbuff group), so press the hotkey again for newly produced units. A health bonus does not heal automatically, so the script also fills the added health.
Trainer_Cheat_smite_enemies_Description: Deals the chosen amount of damage to every enemy unit on the map. A high value acts as a one-key wipeout, but units still follow the normal death sequence and award experience normally.
Trainer_Cheat_explore_all_Description: Reveals the entire map at once (ExploreAll). This cannot be undone, but it does not disable fog of war.
Trainer_Cheat_toggle_fog_Description: Toggles fog of war (ToggleFog). Press repeatedly to switch it off and on.
Trainer_Cheat_spawn_unit_Description: Spawns the chosen number of units, at the chosen level and with the chosen carried items, on the ground under the mouse cursor. Coordinates come from MousePtm(), a function registered in the executable but absent from the official documentation. It returns the map coordinates under the cursor, not screen pixels (those come from a different function, MousePos). The Switchable Units selection determines which unit is spawned; use the Cycle Spawn Unit hotkey in-game to change it immediately without reapplying the trainer. The underlying Place call must receive a point structure (confirmed against stock scripts; incorrectly passing separate x and y integers causes an error in key-bound script). Spawned units begin with full food (20/20) so they do not immediately starve. A configured starting level is applied with SetLevel, and configured carried items are equipped through AddItem. Choosing Full Food Mule spawns a trade mule (Trader) and automatically loads 1000 food by calling Wagon.LoadFood(1000), also at the cursor position.
Trainer_Cheat_cycle_unit_Description: Switches to the next unit in the list and prints its name on screen. The list is the one selected on the Spawn Unit at Cursor row; both actions share one environment variable, so switching requires neither reapplying the trainer nor restarting the game.
Trainer_Cheat_spawn_item_Description: Spawns a bag (DefItemHolder) containing the selected item on the ground under the mouse cursor. Coordinates come from MousePtm(); the bag appears at the cursor position and can be collected by a nearby hero or unit. The Switchable Items selection determines which item is spawned; use the Cycle Spawn Item hotkey in-game to change it immediately without reapplying the trainer. If a quantity is configured, that many copies of the item are placed in the same bag.
Trainer_Cheat_cycle_item_Description: Switches to the next item in the list and prints its name on screen. The list is the one selected on the Spawn Item at Cursor row; both actions share one environment variable, so switching requires neither reapplying the trainer nor restarting the game.
Trainer_Cheat_set_selected_level_Descrip: Sets the currently selected unit or hero directly to the chosen target level (1–1000) and fully heals it to that level's maximum health. If a hero is selected, every soldier in that hero's army is also leveled and fully healed. This calls the engine's undocumented selu() function to obtain the selected object, then sets the level through Unit::SetLevel.
Trainer_Cheat_game_speed_Description: Switches to the next multiplier in the list and prints the current speed on screen. It uses the engine's own SetSpeed() script function. The native baseline is 1000, so n× speed is SetSpeed(n * 1000); the stock scdebug.xml Extreme Speed toggle uses the same function at 10×. Speed is global rather than per-player, so enemy AI and production accelerate too. At very high multipliers the simulation may fail to keep up (see the superlinear slowdown in ISSUES.md ISSUE-005). This is not a trainer fault; switch back to 1× to recover.
Trainer_Cheat_diagnose_Description: Prints the player number and unit count on screen. After installation, press this hotkey first to confirm that hotkeys are active. Script errors are printed in the same location.
Trainer_Tweak_hero_max_army_Description: The number of soldiers one hero can command. Stock value: 50. This is the max_army attribute in data/classes/hero.sc.xml and is shared by all heroes.
Trainer_Tweak_hero_maxhealth_Description: A hero's base maximum health. Stock value: 1000. Level-up bonuses are added on top of this value.
Trainer_Tweak_hero_health_per_level_Desc: Health gained by a hero at each level. Stock value: 20.
Trainer_Tweak_hero_exp_divider_Descripti: Smaller values level heroes faster because army experience is divided by this value. Stock value: 10.
Trainer_Tweak_townhall_maxgold_Descripti: Gold storage cap of a Roman town hall. Stock value: 100000. The Refill Gold hotkey fills a settlement to its current actual cap. Non-stock or explicitly scoped values use .cktw and are applied on every income tick to both existing and newly created settlements. This applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each client applies its own self scope, which desyncs the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_townhall_maxfood_Descripti: Food storage cap of a Roman town hall. Stock value: 100000. Non-stock or explicitly scoped values use .cktw and are applied on every income tick to both existing and newly created settlements. This applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each client applies its own self scope, which desyncs the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_townhall_start_gold_Descri: Starting gold assigned when a town hall is created. Stock value: 2500. This item still affects new settlements only: the .cktw hook runs only when the constructor receives current-gold override -1; explicit values supplied by a map or save bypass it. This applies in single-player and multiplayer alike, and desyncs the simulation in multiplayer.
Trainer_Tweak_townhall_max_population_De: Population cap of one town. Stock value: 100. Non-stock or explicitly scoped values use .cktw and are applied on every income tick to both existing and newly created settlements. This applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each client applies its own self scope, which desyncs the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_village_max_population_Des: Population cap of one village. Stock value: 20. Non-stock or explicitly scoped values use .cktw and are applied on every income tick to both existing and newly created settlements. This applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each client applies its own self scope, which desyncs the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_village_maxgold_Descriptio: Gold storage cap of a Gaul village. Stock value: 5000. Non-stock or explicitly scoped values use .cktw and are applied on every income tick to both existing and newly created settlements. This applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each client applies its own self scope, which desyncs the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_village_maxfood_Descriptio: Food storage cap of a Gaul village. Stock value: 5000. Non-stock or explicitly scoped values use .cktw and are applied on every income tick to both existing and newly created settlements. This applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each client applies its own self scope, which desyncs the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_gold_production_Descriptio: Gold output as a percentage of population. Stock value: 24.
Trainer_Tweak_food_production_Descriptio: Food output as a percentage of population. Stock value: 20.
Trainer_Tweak_pop_growth_rate_Descriptio: Population added during each growth cycle. Stock value: 1.
Trainer_Tweak_pop_growth_interval_Descri: Time between population growth cycles. Stock value: 20000 ms (20 seconds). Smaller values grow faster. Natural growth stops at the population cap and cannot exceed it.
Trainer_Tweak_pop_decrease_interval_Desc: Time between population-loss cycles while population is above the cap. Stock value: 4000 ms (4 seconds). A very large value (for example, 100000000, about 27 hours) effectively disables the loss and lets population added by the Boost Population hotkey remain. This is the key companion setting for that hotkey.
Trainer_Tweak_pop_decrease_percent_Descr: Percentage of the excess population removed during each loss cycle. Stock value: 10. The engine always removes at least 1 point (a hard-coded floor at 0x50270C), so setting this to 0 does not stop the loss; use the loss interval above to retain population.
Trainer_Tweak_train_speed_Description: Divides every training command's duration by this multiplier: ×2 halves production time and doubles speed. Affects 24 training commands in commands.xml (stock durations range from 6 to 300 seconds). Scoped values go into .cktw and take over both script paths that read the duration (the zero-argument Obj::Progress() and Obj::cmddelay), so stock barrack training really is affected. Applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each side applies its own values, which desynchronises the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_research_speed_Description: Divides every research and upgrade command's duration by this multiplier: ×2 halves research time. Affects 41 research commands in commands.xml (stock durations range from 10 to 200 seconds). Scoped values go into .cktw and share the same interception points as production speed. Applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; multiplayer desynchronises the simulation.
Trainer_Tweak_all_unit_health_Descriptio: Scales maxhealth for every class, including buildings. Class definitions are shared by both sides, so computer players of the same faction receive the same bonus. Multiple multipliers are multiplied together.
Trainer_Tweak_all_unit_attack_Descriptio: Scales minattack / maxattack for every unit class. Both sides are affected equally.
Trainer_Tweak_all_unit_defense_Descripti: Scales defense_slash / defense_pierce for every unit class. Both sides are affected equally.
Trainer_Tweak_all_unit_speed_Description: Scales speed for every unit class. Both sides are affected equally.
Trainer_Tweak_gaul_unit_power_Descriptio: Scales health and attack only for units whose class IDs start with G (Gaul). A Gaul computer player becomes stronger too.
Trainer_Tweak_roman_unit_power_Descripti: Scales health and attack only for units whose class IDs start with R (Roman).
Trainer_Tweak_unit_feeds_Description: 0 means that side's units no longer draw food from settlements; 1 is the stock default. Scoped values go into .cktw and take over the two Settlement::TakeResource call sites where the engine actually deducts food (units attached to a settlement, and units foraging in the field). When a deduction is skipped the unit is still fed the same amount, so it never starves or loses health, while the settlement's stores are left untouched. Unit build costs and wagon loading are unaffected. The class file's feeds attribute (data/classes/unit.sc.xml) only gates the engine's starvation behaviour, not the food economy, so it is no longer used to apply this setting (ISSUE-071). Applies in single-player and multiplayer alike; in multiplayer each side applies its own values, which desynchronises the simulation.

Gui_Profiler_ModeLaunch: Let the toolkit start the game
Gui_Profiler_ModeLaunchDesc: The most complete option: the diagnostics layer is in place before the game's entry point, so recording covers the very first millisecond. Requires a valid game folder above.
Gui_Profiler_ModeAttachDesc: Pick this when the game is already open. Recording starts the moment you press Start; anything before that is lost.
Gui_Profiler_ModeWait: Press Start, then launch from Steam as usual
Gui_Profiler_ModeWaitDesc: The toolkit waits in the background and attaches the instant the game appears. Choose this if you normally start from Steam - no need to change how you launch just to get a recording.
Gui_Profiler_SecondsDesc: 0 keeps recording until the game exits or you press Stop. Leave it at 0 when chasing a crash that happens at an unpredictable time.
Gui_Profiler_HzDesc: How many times per second each game thread's EIP is sampled. Higher is more detailed but can affect game performance; the default 250 is enough for most problems.
Gui_Profiler_SegmentDesc: How often the running hot-spot summary is recomputed. Only affects the segmented summary in the final report, not the per-second log.
Gui_Profiler_DetailedDesc: Records every thread's registers, a stack scan, and memory/resource usage each second. Turning this off leaves only a coarse segment summary, missing the detail that actually helps diagnose a crash.
Gui_Profiler_CatchCrashDesc: Freezes the scene the instant an exception is raised and writes a minidump plus a JSON state snapshot. This is the only way to catch cases where the engine swallows the exception and exits with a misleadingly clean exit code.
Gui_Profiler_FullDump: Include full memory in the dump (very large)
Gui_Profiler_FullDumpDesc: Adds the process's full memory to the minidump, typically 1-2 GB. Good for deep analysis in WinDbg, but uses a lot of disk space.
Gui_Profiler_SpeedDesc: Speeds up reproduction of problems that only show up after a long time, without modifying any game file. Speed is restored automatically when profiling stops.
Gui_Profiler_SpeedMethodDesc: "Vanilla keys" is safest, fixed at the factory turbo speed (10x). "Built-in console" can set any multiplier but you'll see it typed into the console input line. Both bring the game window to the foreground before sending keys.
Gui_Profiler_LogFolderDesc: Choose a storage location (the Desktop by default). The toolkit creates a CKToolkit 分析紀錄 folder, then organizes it by date and individual run, so logs, dumps, and JSON files never spill across the Desktop. Both diagnostic layers for one run remain together.
Gui_Profiler_SelectOutput: Choose where analysis records are stored
Gui_Profiler_Hint: One recording runs both layers at once: the in-game diagnostics layer covers per-frame timing and memory telemetry, the external debugger writes a minidump and a JSON state snapshot at the moment of a crash, and the sampler adds the per-second full state plus EIP hot spots. Both layers write to the same folder. Pick "How to Start" below, then press Start.
Gui_Profiler_LayerRuntimeEarly: active (before the entry point, the whole run is covered)
Gui_Profiler_LayerRuntimeLate: active (attached, events from the first seconds are missing)
Gui_Profiler_LayerRuntimeOff: not active ({0}); this run only has the sampler and debugger records
Gui_Profiler_RunHint: Press Stop, or Esc, at any time. Stopping ends the recording only - it does not close the game.
Profile_Crashed: The game exited by crashing, exit code {0}.
Gui_Profiler_Complete: Diagnostics run finished and produced a report.

Gui_Log_ScriptChannelReady: The trainer script channel was requested. Open the in-game panel to trigger every cheat directly, with no key binding needed.

Gui_About_Description: One Windows GUI for the Steam edition of Celtic Kings: Rage of War, integrating performance compatibility, HD support, extensible localization, file-based cheats, save and player-data management, and a sampling profiler.
Gui_About_Features:
Modules: Performance · Language packs · Trainer · Profiler
Interface: English and Traditional Chinese · Agent-facing non-interactive CLI
Gui_About_Safety: No game-file backup copies are created. Every recognised toolkit patch carries an exact reversal path; unknown or third-party-modified files are refused and must be restored with Steam file verification.
Gui_About_License: Open source under the MIT License. Target: Steam CK_RageOfWar (2004).

GameSettings_Subtitle: Customize unit traits, hero army attachment rules, and gameplay mechanics. Safely applied to data.pak and fully reversible.
GameSettings_AllowVikingLordHeroArmy_Lab: Allow Viking Lords in hero armies
GameSettings_AllowVikingLordHeroArmy_Des: Removes the 'Freedom' restriction from Viking Lords, allowing heroes to attach them into formations and share EXP while keeping vampire blow.
GameSettings_AllowLiberatiHeroArmy_Desc: Removes the 'Freedom' restriction from Liberati, allowing heroes to attach them into formations and share EXP while keeping trample damage.
GameSettings_AllowMuleHeroArmy_Label: Allow food mules in hero armies
GameSettings_AllowMuleHeroArmy_Desc: Removes the right-click follow restriction from pack mules and adds central formation protection, allowing heroes to attach them for marching and on-the-go feeding.
Error_SettingsSubcommandRequired: The settings command requires a 'get' or 'set' subcommand.
GameSettings_WagonCapacity10k_Desc: Increases mule payload capacity to 10,000, and updates the large food/gold mule production buttons and loading commands to 10,000.
